title: A method for building a federated learning architecture that integrates blockchain state sharding and reputation mechanisms

pse.problem: Traditional federated learning has issues of single point of failure for centralized gradient aggregation server and low efficiency due to synchronous training. Also, traditional blockchains have low throughput, storage scalability is low, and federated learning nodes and blockchain nodes are isolated.
pse.solution_function: The method constructs a decentralized federated learning architecture by integrating blockchain state sharding and reputation mechanisms. It distributes nodes into shards, trains local models using local data within each shard, aggregates local models to form global models within the shard, and performs inter-shard consensus to select an inter-shard master node that uploads the model to the main chain and aggregates it to obtain a new global model.
pse.solution_structure: The architecture consists of nodes divided into shards, each shard having a sub-chain, a master node, and other participating nodes. The main chain serves as the final storage for the aggregated global model.
pse.solution_implementation: The process involves grouping nodes into shards, sending the initial model to each node in a shard, training local models using local data, broadcasting local models within the shard, aggregating local models to form a global model within the shard, and performing inter-shard consensus to select an inter-shard master node. The reputation mechanism is used to assign weights to local models during aggregation.
pse.effect: The solution aims to solve the problems of low throughput in traditional blockchains, low storage scalability, and isolation between federated learning nodes and blockchain nodes, by implementing decentralized federated learning using blockchain state sharding and reputation mechanisms.
